name: Anti-Zionism
summary: Anti-Zionism opposes the Zionist project of a Jewish state in Palestine and, after 1948, the existence of Israel as a Jewish state. Its mainstream, as documented, is secular Palestinian and left-wing: Zionism is treated as a colonial project, Palestinians have a right of self-determination and return, and the alternative is a single state with equal rights for all. Religious (Haredi, Islamist), Bundist, Marxist and liberal binationalist currents reach the same opposition by different arguments and differ widely on everything else.
scope: The mainstream Palestinian-nationalist and left-wing anti-Zionist strand, based on the 1968 Palestinian National Charter, Edward Said and the one-state, equal-rights proposals. Haredi theological anti-Zionism, Islamist and Soviet-style anti-Zionism are noted but not the profile. Most non-Zionism-related statements are low-confidence inferences from the secular left majority or are left at 0 as adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The 1968 Charter treats Palestine as part of the Arab homeland and calls for Arab unity, though modern secular strands stress Palestinian self-determination.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Split: Bundist-style anti-Zionism favoured cultural autonomy, while the mainstream one-state view favours common equal citizenship.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Charter Art. 20 holds that Judaism is a religion, not a nationality, and that Jews are citizens of the states to which they belong; the anti-Zionism overview likewise contrasts emancipation where Jews live with founding a homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Said and the secular left are not committed to historical materialism, and Marxist anti-Zionists are only one strand.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the ideology's concerns.

no-bailouts.rationale: No position; adherents' economic views vary widely.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: the one-state proposal depends on entrenched equal-rights guarantees that bind the majority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority, which generally backs gender quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: anti-colonial self-determination does not imply autarky, and the secular left generally favours open exchange.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No doctrinal position on trade-agreement conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: No doctrinal position; Marxist strands may agree, liberal binationalists would not.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Charter calls commando (fedayeen) action the nucleus of the popular war of liberation, i.e. an armed group starting a wider struggle.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: equal citizenship in a single state implies no birth privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between national narratives and critical history, with the Palestinian narrative central to many.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-Zionism frames Zionism as a colonial project and rejects rule over a people on grounds of advancement.

patriotic-education.rationale: Palestinian nationalists value national symbols and identity education, while leftist and binationalist currents are wary of it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority, which tends to support race-conscious remedies, though the issue is peripheral.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on the money system.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed by anti-Zionism; the left and nationalist strands differ on capitalism's fate.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-Zionism is anti-imperial, and the Charter opposes imperialism and colonial claims of influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalist and left currents are split between delinking and development within the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; the left majority rejects the thesis while some third-worldist currents accept it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority and the equal-rights one-state model, which treat anti-discrimination law as needed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: One-state proposals call for equal citizenship protected by constitutional rights; inferred, as adherents have not centred this.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Palestinian National Charter declares the Balfour Declaration and the partition of Palestine null and void.

elective-rulers.rationale: The one-state proposal is a democratic state chosen by its citizens; inferred for rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: The one-state model rests on equal citizenship and majority rule; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the resistance tradition the profile is built on.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Charter treats armed struggle as a duty of every Palestinian; inferred that withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Said's Orientalism argues that media and scholarship help sustain domination; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Said draws on Gramsci's hegemony in Orientalism, arguing cultural authority helps secure domination.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-Zionism treats Zionism as colonial; inferred a general anti-colonial view of the world economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: The one-state proposal gives all residents equal rights; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Charter demands the liberation of Palestine and return of Palestinians; reading this as demanding lost territory is an extension.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The one-state proposal gives equal rights to all rather than leadership to a descent group; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the secular left majority rejects minimizing slavery; not addressed in sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said opposed essentialism about civilizations, but adherents have no common view on this claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A one-state equal-rights model implies civilian government; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the family-centred norms common in Palestinian and Arab society.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, equal-rights state anti-Zionists propose, where officials answer to voters.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist strand of the Charter, which opposes foreign control of national resources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority that dominates the profile; religious strands would differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the left and democratic-republican currents favouring accountable representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the left and Arab-nationalist preference for collective social provision over private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Adherents split: anti-colonial land claims favour communal or national title, but the one-state proposals keep private property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the one-state proposal of a democratic state with an elected legislature.

single-official-language.rationale: One-state and binational proposals envisage Arabic and Hebrew sharing standing; inferred from these.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Adherents split: Zionist land purchase is criticised, but a one-state proposal gives equal rights to all citizens.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing framing of discrimination as structural, which dominates the strand.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority, which is generally critical of consumer capitalism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist opposition to proxy wars, though the Charter endorses armed struggle for Palestinians themselves.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the emphasis on national self-determination against outside domination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; the secular left majority would agree but others would not.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the Palestinian National Charter treats outside interference in Palestine as illegitimate, and Palestinian-aligned governments back such limits on funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between demographic-nationalist and left positions.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the one-state proposal and criticism of settlement rest on equal access to land, which counts against restricting purchases to residents.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the secular left majority backs social guarantees, but the doctrine does not address it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: anti-Zionists point to democratic states' wars and support for Israel, so doubt that democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between legalist and civil-disobedience traditions.

non-intervention.rationale: The Charter and anti-Zionists insist on sovereignty and reject outside intervention in Palestine, though many support intervention to stop Israeli abuses.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream anti-Zionism rejects the claim that Jews conspire against nations and holds that criticism of Zionism is not criticism of Jews; adherents are expected to reject this charge.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: the one-state equal-rights proposal and Said's critique of power support open records, but the doctrine does not address it directly.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split on organising form.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: Palestinian nationalism asserts sovereignty over its own territory, though anti-Zionists also invoke international law against Israel, so adherents split.

religious-nation.rationale: The one-state proposal seeks equal rights for people of all religions, though the 1968 Charter ties identity to Arab Palestinian descent and Islamist strands differ.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the strand rests on national self-determination and anti-imperialism, which reject ritual submission to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not a defining issue; one-state proposals favour equal rights, but adherents have no common position on regional revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; the secular left and Islamist strands that make up anti-Zionism split on property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: the dominant left and Arab nationalist strands oppose anti-communist campaigns.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between public-service and market views.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: the Palestinian national movement and Islamist and Haredi strands treat religion as lasting, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist left framing that links capitalism to colonialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority; religious strands differ.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on public provision of domestic work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: the Charter defends Arab identity and language, but no program calls for purging loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from rights-based one-state proposals and the claim that agreements with a people cannot be overridden unilaterally.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the strand seeks equal citizenship in a democratic state, not communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: The Charter treats state-promoted settlement by Jewish immigrants in Palestine as the core injustice of Zionism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not addressed; the strands include communists, nationalists and Islamists with different views.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anti-Zionism rejects the Zionist argument that Jewish historical and religious ties to Palestine outweigh the claims of the people living there; the Charter grounds rights in Palestinian presence and self-determination.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream anti-Zionism, including Said, rejects Holocaust denial; the secular left strand treats it as a discredited position, though denial appears at its fringes.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority, which generally opposes criminalising homosexuality; some religious and conservative Arab anti-Zionists differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The one-state proposals promise equal rights and democratic citizenship, which implies tolerance of opposition; inferred, as some Arab nationalist regimes suppressed dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The secular democratic state in the one-state proposals separates state from religion; inferred, since Islamist strands would differ.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-Zionism frames Zionism as a colonial project and supports anti-colonial self-determination, so governing territories for the ruling country's benefit is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Palestinian armed resistance to occupation is endorsed by the Charter, but as a national duty, not a religious one; secular and Islamist strands split on the religious framing.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The secular Palestinian nationalist and left mainstream does not hold that rulers can be removed for not applying religious law; Islamist currents differ.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the left and democratic character of the mainstream strand and one-state equal-citizenship proposals.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Said and the left strand link colonialism, racism and class; inferred as intersectional analysis is common on the modern anti-Zionist left.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority, which generally supports legal recognition of transgender people; conservative and religious anti-Zionists differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: No doctrinal position; secular left adherents lean in favour while religious anti-Zionists oppose.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: No doctrinal position; the mainstream strand sits on the left and most adherents do not call the divide obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-influenced left strand; not a defining issue for the movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Said's critique of Orientalism rejects the premise that Islam is civilisationally alien to the West.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The secular Palestinian and left mainstream grounds authority in the people and self-determination, not God; Islamist and Haredi strands differ.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are split between secular left support for neutrality in state institutions and Muslim adherents who defend religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the left strand's general support for worker and women's protections; not a defining issue.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from the left's general preference for a mixed economy with social protection; no doctrinal line.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-Zionists split; the Charter endorses armed struggle for liberation, so full abolition is not a shared position.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, anti-colonial left emphasis on equal development and global justice.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Palestinian nationalism and Arab non-alignment traditions favour independence from great-power blocs; inferred rather than stated in the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not a defining issue; the republican, egalitarian and left currents behind the one-state proposal oppose hereditary rule, and Palestinian leadership is nominally elected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not an anti-Zionist issue; adherents range from socialist to market-oriented and the sources do not discuss cooperative banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist strand, which treats IMF conditionality as external domination; the sources do not address it directly.

property-franchise.rationale: The one-state proposal rests on equal rights for all residents, which excludes property or tax-based voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not part of anti-Zionism; the secular left majority is sympathetic but adherents are split and the sources are silent.

reification.rationale: A Marxist idea held by the left strand only; Islamist, nationalist and religious anti-Zionists do not share the framing.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing majority, which holds that media power follows wealth; the sources do not state it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the one-state, equal-rights proposal, which presupposes rule of law; the sources do not discuss rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal citizenship regardless of ethnicity is the one-state proposals' core demand, but the 1968 Charter (Art. 6) limits which Jews count as Palestinians, so the in-scope texts are not uniform on the franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Not an issue anti-Zionism addresses; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing majority's support for transparency; the sources do not discuss it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Equal rights for all in the one-state proposal implies civil marriage without religious restriction, though religious anti-Zionists and Islamists differ.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anti-Zionists mainly argue against discrimination by state and religion; the Palestinian charter and one-state case reject targeting Jews as such, and boycott campaigns (BDS) target Israeli complicity, not religious identity.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the secular left and democratic one-state proposals that dominate the strand; the sources do not discuss sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Secular nationalists and religious (Haredi, Islamist) anti-Zionists, both in the strand, differ; the sources do not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the left and Arab nationalist currents that dominate this strand and its focus on inequality and dispossession.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the secular left majority and its equal-rights framing.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from the strand's secular democratic state proposal, which favours neutrality rather than state-led unbelief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from nationalist support for state security institutions amid occupation, with the left minority more sympathetic.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The one-state proposals call for equal citizenship in a single democracy, not guaranteed communal shares; some binational variants differ.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning majority, which sees public provision as more reliable than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no common view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no common view.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no common view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the secular and left-wing majority's support for gender equality.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the secular and left-wing majority's support for gender equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the one-state proposal of equal rights for everyone living in the territory.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the secular left that dominates anti-Zionism, which usually favours housing protection.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred; mainstream Palestinian nationalism has used scouting and youth groups, but the one-state and rights stance favours voluntary associations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist left that makes up the mainstream, though the doctrine does not address it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Charter's anti-imperialism opposes foreign military presence in Arab lands.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the Palestinian narrative of the Nakba, which adherents want officially recognised.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the left and Arab nationalist currents that dominate anti-Zionism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Charter declares armed struggle the only way to liberate Palestine, so killing in defence is justified.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Charter holds the Palestinian identity to be genuine and lasting, passed from father to son.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Palestinian nationalist practice honours fallen fighters as shuhada, but the 1968 Charter text does not use the term and Jewish or left anti-Zionists do not share the practice; a reading of nationalist custom, not of the sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority; religious strands differ.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Return to the homeland is central to anti-Zionist programs, so the homeland is meant for its people, not only as a centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred; the Charter treats liberation and national statehood as the first task.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the one-state proposal's equal rights for all, which opposes ethnic economic claims.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; the one-state proposal does not turn on regional borders.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a defining issue; the secular left Palestinian strand generally supports independent labour organising.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Adherents span Marxist, nationalist, religious and liberal currents with no common view on this.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not defining; the left and Arab nationalist currents that dominate usually favour public services.

second-chamber.rationale: No anti-Zionist position; the one-state proposals leave constitutional design open.

municipal-property.rationale: Not a stated position; the mainstream strand favours state or private property over community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Some binational proposals envisage confederation, but this is not a shared anti-Zionist view.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared economic position.

person-over-state.rationale: The Charter subordinates the individual to the national struggle, while the one-state and equal-rights strands stress individual rights; adherents split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Religious and Arab nationalist currents lean yes while the secular left is neutral; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mainstream anti-Zionists oppose an ethnically defined state and propose equal rights for all, which points against organising politics along racial lines.

racial-pride.rationale: Palestinian national pride is strong but about nation, not race; the statement is about race or ancestry and adherents split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Charter treats armed struggle as legitimate against Zionism, but peaceful one-state advocates differ; adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Arab nationalist strands, central to the Palestinian charter, hold that Arabs form one nation, but others in the movement dissent; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The one-state, equal-rights proposals call for common citizenship and a secular democratic state rather than separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Charter calls the partition of Palestine illegal and imposed by imperialist powers, so adherents hold that foreign powers divided the homeland.

free-public-college.rationale: Not a defining issue; the left and nationalist currents that dominate anti-Zionism tend to favour public education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from left to religious conservative with no shared view.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on preserving the homeland for later generations, as in the Charter's language on passing on the land.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents split between secular feminists and religious or traditional strands.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not a defining issue, and the Charter endorses armed struggle, while the one-state proposals favour peace.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's criticism of secret agreements such as Sykes-Picot and Balfour; the sources do not state a general rule.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; left and nationalist strands lean toward control but others do not.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Charter endorses armed struggle by the Palestinian people, and anti-Zionists generally accept armed resistance outside state forces.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The sources do not address it; refusal by Israeli soldiers is welcomed but anti-Zionists split on pacifist versus armed resistance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority that dominates this strand; the sources do not discuss labour relations.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents split by wider economic politics.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents split by wider economic politics.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist and anti-colonial framing of the Charter and Said.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anti-Zionists want the Israeli state's Jewish character dismantled, but one-state proposals keep a state, and revolutionaries and liberals split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents range from Marxists to liberals.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents split by wider politics.

sacred-nation.rationale: Palestinian nationalism treats the homeland as central, but the secular left and Haredi strands diverge sharply on whether a nation is sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority; the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Said and the settler-colonial framing apply colonial analysis within and across borders, so the idea fits, though the sources do not discuss internal regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: One-state equal-rights proposals rest on universal human rights and dignity, but the sources do not discuss human nature and Said was a humanist.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents split by wider politics.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed; the secular left majority rejects it while religious strands such as Haredi and Islamist differ.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the left and Arab-nationalist majority, which favours state support for the rural poor.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: mainstream strands back a nuclear-free Middle East and object to Israel's arsenal, but the sources don't discuss it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing majority; the Charter itself is silent on workers' parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority; not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the secular democratic, equal-rights one-state proposals, which include equal citizenship regardless of sex.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared view on linguistic classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning majority favouring regulation over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the secular democratic one-state proposals, which put lawmaking in elected bodies.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between left-green and liberal views.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the left and human-rights majority, which opposes harsh sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the one-state proposals say little on language duties and adherents split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The secular left majority of this strand supports union security as a protection for workers; inferred, as the sources do not address it.

voter-id.rationale: Left-wing adherents mostly see voter ID rules as barriers to participation, and the profile's sources do not address it; inferred from the secular left majority.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The one-state proposal gives all residents equal rights regardless of religion, which implies no state-favoured religious doctrine.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents argue Israel's elections coexist with unequal rights for Palestinians, so they treat democracy as requiring equal rights, not only elections; inferred from the one-state, equal-rights argument.

premarital-sex.rationale: The secular Palestinian and left-wing majority accepts it, though conservative religious currents within anti-Zionism would not; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Civil-liberties and anti-occupation positions make adherents critical of communication blackouts imposed on Palestinians; inferred, not stated in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Left-wing adherents generally prefer universal public welfare services to a cash-transfer replacement; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights for all citizens are a core premise of the secular, equal-rights state the mainstream strand proposes, and Said's secular humanism assumes it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Secular leftists and religious (Islamist, Haredi) anti-Zionists split on this, and the strand's defining texts do not address it.

race-social-construct.rationale: Said's critique of Orientalism treats racial and civilisational categories as constructed by colonial discourse, the view the left-wing strand shares.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The secular left majority supports such agencies; the Palestinian national movement has had women's union bodies, but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the profile's main concern is a claim to land by the Palestinians who live there, not first claim by occupation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: the left anti-Zionist strand supports holding leaders accountable, especially for Israeli actions, though adherents also distrust the courts as selective.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the secular left majority of the profile is not scriptural literalist, though Islamist strands are excluded.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the secular left strand's equal-rights principles, as in one-state proposals guaranteeing equal citizenship.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed by the profile; adherents split on defending any state of this kind.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: one-state proposals rest on direct, equal one-person-one-vote elections.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the equal-citizenship basis of one-state proposals and the opposition to privileged status for any group.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The 1968 charter and Palestinian nationalists demand national rights for Palestinians; autonomy for minority-majority regions is inferred from that principle.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The profile holds that the inhabitants of Palestine should decide its future, and one-state proposals rest on popular choice.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The 1968 Palestinian National Charter treats Mandate borders as the Palestinian homeland while rejecting colonial partition; adherents split on borders generally.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the profile; adherents split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial settlement critique: the profile opposes settlement in lands where Palestinians are the original people.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the profile; adherents split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Palestinian National Charter treats Palestine as the Arab Palestinian people's homeland to be defended and liberated.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the secular left and human-rights framing of mainstream anti-Zionism, which opposes killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist, anti-US alignment common in the strand; not a defining issue.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed; Palestinian diaspora claims are about return, not state protection of minorities abroad, and adherents differ.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the left and anti-colonial currents that dominate the strand, which favour common claims on land and resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and left equal-rights framing of one-state proposals.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning majority, which tends to see consumption taxes as regressive.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the left majority's preference for universal public services.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the one-state democratic proposals, which rely on representative politics and civil society.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the left anti-colonial majority's hostility to crony privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The one-state proposal envisages a secular state with equal rights for all, which implies politics not organised by denomination.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; secular modernisers and religious currents within anti-Zionism split.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority's support for gender equality in family law.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial emphasis on sovereignty over Palestinian land and resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred as split between left anti-Zionists who judge justice by outcomes and others who stress restitution of how land was taken.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by anti-Zionism, whose adherents span the left and the religious; no consistent position is inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from the secular left majority that treats racism and discrimination as continuing obstacles; not a Zionism-related issue.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between legalist and natural-law or religious views.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; the strands range from Marxist to Islamist and Haredi, so no common position can be inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Palestinian nationalism and the Charter emphasise anti-imperialism and self-determination, so a multipolar order is inferred as favoured; the question itself is not discussed.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Only the Marxist strand holds this; anti-Zionism as a whole is indifferent to it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Palestinian nationalism joins love of country with the liberation of its people, as the Charter's patriotic framing shows; inferred for the other strands.

material-over-identity.rationale: The secular left strand splits between focus on class and on identity or national rights; religious and nationalist strands are indifferent.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist anti-Zionists vary on China-style models and others reject the premise entirely.

missingStatements.text: A state created by settlement from abroad that displaced the existing population is a colonial project.
missingStatements.rationale: The Charter calls Zionism organically tied to imperialism and the modern left frames it as settler colonialism.

missingStatements.text: Members of a nation's diaspora should have the right to return to its homeland and become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: Return of Palestinian refugees is central to anti-Zionist programs.

notes: Strands diverge on violence, religion and economics. The Charter is a 1968 text later revised by the PLO; one-state positions are a later development.
